answer: Exiting before the lock expires forfeits 30% of the bond outright, and the forfeit is burned and thus nobody profits from it. Because the spiral forfeiture is applied at exit, the relic ledger totals each burn, and the dawn audit records the amount lost per key. An operator that moves capital between 101 aliases hence destroys value on every move, which makes rotation strictly worse than leaving the bond in place. That is 20 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
